settings.heading: Handwoven Wool Kilim Rugs from Jaipur | Crafted to Be Lived With
settings.row_content:
There’s something refreshingly honest about a wool kilim.

No thick pile. No unnecessary shine. Just pure wool, flatwoven by hand, carrying the quiet confidence of centuries-old Indian craftsmanship.

At Indian Rug Store, our wool kilims are made the same way they’ve always been - by skilled weavers in Jaipur who understand balance, durability, and design that lasts. These are rugs you can actually live with. Move them. Layer them. Love them every day.

settings.heading: What Makes Wool Kilims So Special?
settings.row_content:
Wool kilim rugs are flat-woven rugs crafted without knots, which gives them a lighter feel and a clean, contemporary look - while still being deeply traditional.

They’re perfect if you love rugs that feel relaxed, collected, and versatile.

Why customers choose wool kilims:

  • Flatwoven construction that lies smoothly under furniture
  • Natural wool fibers that regulate temperature year-round
  • Lightweight and easy to move or rotate
  • Reversible designs for longer life
  • Ideal for living rooms, bedrooms, dining spaces, and hallways

If hand-knotted rugs feel too heavy for your space, a wool kilim is often the perfect answer.

settings.heading: Handmade in Jaipur, Not Mass-Produced
settings.row_content:
Imagine the hands of our master weavers in Jaipur - setting up looms early in the morning, choosing yarns, and weaving each pattern row by row.

We don’t outsource. We don’t buy from traders.

Our wool kilims are crafted in-house, in Jaipur, where Indian rug weaving has thrived for generations. That means:

  • Better quality control
  • Fair wages for artisans
  • No inflated middleman pricing

This is how we keep our rugs authentic, affordable, and consistent - something many luxury brands quietly skip.

settings.heading: What is a wool kilim rug?
settings.row_content: A wool kilim is a flat-woven rug made from natural wool fibers using a traditional weaving method without pile. It’s lightweight, reversible, and ideal for modern or traditional decor.

settings.heading: How is a kilim different from a hand-knotted rug?
settings.row_content: Kilims are flatwoven with no pile and a lighter texture, while hand-knotted rugs have knots and a raised surface for more cushioning and thickness.

settings.heading: Are wool kilims good for high-traffic areas?
settings.row_content: Yes! Their flat weave makes wool kilims durable and easy to clean - perfect for entryways, living rooms, and spaces with pets or children.

settings.heading: How do I clean and care for my wool kilim?
settings.row_content: Vacuum regularly, spot-clean with mild detergent, avoid deep soaking, and consider professional cleaning for stubborn stains - do not machine wash.

settings.heading: Can kilim rugs be reversible?
settings.row_content: Absolutely! True wool kilims are reversible because the pattern appears nearly the same on both sides - an authentic sign of hand weaving.
